in_text_mentions: examination, endoscopy with finding of gastrointestinal polyposis, and histology. CCS is characterised by diffuse multiple polyps of the gastrointestinal tract, diarrhoea, weight loss, abdominal pain, cutaneous hyperpigmentation, dystrophic involvement of fingernails, and alopecia (Figures 1(a), 1(b), 2, and 3). Other symptoms such as hypogeusia and xerostomia have also been described in the literature [6]. Dysgeusia can be caused by mucositis, oral infections, and other abnormalities of mucosal surface. Zinc and copper deficiencies are also believed to cause hypogeusia in some patients [14].

plate_findings.evidence: Caption describes diffuse polypoid and granular elevations with surface redness throughout the colon and rectum; panel A shows polypoid mucosal elevations in the descending colon.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A is a real colonoscopy image from a patient with Cronkhite-Canada syndrome showing diffuse colonic polypoid mucosal changes characteristic of gastrointestinal polyposis. B: Panel B is a real colonoscopy image showing multiple reddish, polypoid, wide-based mucosal lesions in the ascending colon, supporting diffuse gastrointestinal polyposis in Cronkhite-Canada syndrome. C: Panel C is a real colonoscopy image demonstrating diffuse granular and polypoid mucosal elevations in the transverse colon, consistent with the characteristic colonic polyposis of Cronkhite-Canada syndrome. D: Panel D is a real endoscopic image of the ileocecal part showing diffuse granular, erythematous, and polypoid mucosal change, supporting the diffuse gastrointestinal polyposis of Cronkhite-Canada syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Wang et al. Cronkhite-Canada syndrome: A case report and literature review.. Medicine 2024. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000040242. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: (A–D) The distal ileum mucosa shows mucosal congestion with scattered multiple polypoid elevations characterized by redness and soft biopsy texture. The mucosa of the entire colon and rectum exhibits diffuse polypoid and granular elevations with surface redness and scattered whitening changes. Some have a strawberry-like appearance characterized by oval or finger-shaped shapes, wide base, and inconspicuous stalk. They are distributed diffusely and carpet-like. The mucosal surface appears congested and swollen, and biopsy samples from different locations have a soft consistency. They vary in size, with the smaller ones measuring 4 mm and the larger ones measuring 20 mm.
in_text_mentions: Colonoscopy revealed diffuse polypoid, granular elevations, a reddish surface on the entire colonic and rectal mucosa, scattered surface whitening changes, polyps of varying sizes, and some with a strawberry-like appearance, ranging in size from 4 mm to 20 mm. The polyps were oval, digitate, with a wide base, lacked a pedicle, had unclear boundaries with the mucosa, and the head end was congested and edematous (Fig. 3).
